key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with optimized DDFW parameters substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, while deep learning can predict tensile performance from process settings.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical joint-design and process-optimization pathway for stronger lightweight aluminum connections in aerospace and automotive manufacturing.
method: Used an L18 orthogonal array to test friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying-surface geometry, and friction time.
Compared conventional flat-to-flat and drilled-to-bossed geometries in direct drive friction welding on a customized engine lathe.
Trained deep learning models to predict ultimate tensile strength from welding conditions.
evidence_signal: The best setup (30 MPa friction pressure, 70 MPa forging pressure, 2200 rpm, drilled-to-bossed geometry, 4 min friction time) achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength; the ensemble residual network reached R² ≈ 0.81.
watch_item: The predictive model performance is moderate rather than definitive, so broader datasets and validation on additional joint geometries and alloys would be needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
